git.name: git_get_context
git.description: Start here for any coding or review task: current branch, upstream ahead/behind, remote URL, recent commits, working tree status, diff stat summary, and Jira keys detected in the branch name. Pass includeDiff=true to also include the full uncommitted diff. Pass fromRef (and optionally toRef) instead to get a diff between two refs or commits, paged with maxChars/charOffset.

repoPath.description: Path to the git repository (defaults to cwd)

commitLimit.description: Number of recent commits to show (default 10)

fromRef.description: Base ref or commit — switches the tool to diff mode (branch vs main, a commit range)

toRef.description: Target ref or commit for diff mode (defaults to the working tree)

maxChars.description: Diff mode: max characters to return (default 8000). Increase for large diffs.

charOffset.description: Diff mode: skip this many characters from the start (for paging large diffs)

context.name: get_dev_context
context.description: Master entry point for "what am I working on / what's the status", and before any review or coding task. Returns: git branch + upstream state, Jira ticket overview (status, transitions, sprint, comments), open PR with reviewer approvals, and actionable next-step hints (create PR, merge, address blockers).

repoPath.description: Local path to the git repo (defaults to cwd)

context.name: get_attachment
context.description: Fetch an attachment by ID and return its contents inline. source=jira for a Jira issue attachment (IDs come from jira_get), source=bitbucket for a repo attachment referenced from a PR description or comment as attachment:<id> (IDs come from bitbucket_get_pr). Images are auto-resized + re-encoded; text/JSON/XML return as text; videos and animated images (GIF/APNG/animated WebP) are decoded with ffmpeg into sampled frames (re-call with start/end/frames or mode=scenes to refine); audio returns as an audio block; PDFs return extracted text. Oversized/non-renderable files are saved to a temp file and the path returned.

source.description: Where the attachment lives. Optional when only one of Jira/Bitbucket is configured.

saveTo.description: Optional absolute path to save the original (un-resized) file to disk instead of returning inline

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (source=bitbucket; overrides workspace roots)

maxDimension.description: Max long-edge size in pixels for inline images (default 1568 for images, 768 for video frames).

quality.description: JPEG quality for re-encoded inline images (1-100, default 85 for images, 65 for video frames). Ignored for images with alpha (encoded as PNG).

frames.description: Video/animated-image only: number of frames to sample (default 6, range 1-60). Higher = more detail + more context.

start.description: Video/animated-image only: start of sample window in seconds (default 0). Use with end/frames to zoom into a moment of interest after a coarse first pass.

end.description: Video/animated-image only: end of sample window in seconds (default full duration). Must be greater than start.

mode.description: Video/animated-image only: "uniform" samples N frames evenly (default); "scenes" uses ffmpeg scene-change detection, better for screencasts/narrative content.

sceneThreshold.description: Video/animated-image only: scene-change sensitivity in 0-1 (default 0.3). Only used when mode=scenes. Lower = more frames, higher = fewer.

jira.name: start_work
jira.description: Start working on a Jira ticket end-to-end: resolves the ticket (by key or free-text search with a picker when multiple match), creates a local branch with an auto-generated name, fetches the project README from Bitbucket so you have commit/PR conventions in context, and prints a next-steps summary. If issueKey is omitted, provide query for free-text search.

issueKey.description: Jira issue key, e.g. FOO-123 (provide this OR query)

query.description: Free-text search when issueKey is unknown — shows a picker if multiple tickets match

baseBranch.description: Branch to base off. Defaults to the repository default branch, resolved from origin/HEAD or, failing that, from Bitbucket. The branch actually used is named in the result.

transitionName.description: Jira transition to apply, e.g. "In Progress" (optional)

push.description: Push branch to remote after creation (default false)

jira.name: jira_search
jira.description:
Discover Jira resources (tickets, projects, boards, sprints, versions, users). Set resource:
• "issues" (default) — search by text, JQL, project, status, assignee, issue type, or mine=true for your queue
• "projects" — list all projects and their keys
• "issue_types" — valid types and statuses for a project
• "boards" — list boards (pass project to filter by project key); use this to find the boardId before fetching sprints or board_overview
• "sprints" — sprints for a board (pass boardId, or project to have the board resolved when it is unambiguous)
• "board_overview" — active/future sprints with their issues for a board (pass boardId, or project to have the board resolved); use when asked "what's in the sprint", "show me the board", or "what's everyone working on"
• "versions" — list fix versions/releases for a project (pass project; optionally pass query to filter by name substring). If the version you need does not exist, create it yourself with `jira_mutate version.action=create version.name=9.1.0` — do NOT ask the user to make it in the Jira UI.
• "components" — list component names for a project (pass project; optionally query to filter). Use this to find valid component names before setting jira_mutate create/update.components.
• "fields" — what jira_mutate customFields can set. Pass project + issueType for a create screen, or issueKey for an existing issue: returns that screen's required and optional fields, each with the value to send and, for selects, the allowed values. With neither, only the instance-wide custom field list. Use this instead of guessing a field id or telling the user to set it in the Jira UI.
• "users" — find users by name/email (pass query)

mine.description: Return issues assigned to you (resource=issues only)

query.description: Text search or user name query

jql.description: Raw JQL (resource=issues only, overrides other filters)

project.description: Project key filter or scope for issue_types/boards

status.description: Status filter (issues only, or board_overview to filter issues by status)

assignee.description: Assignee username filter (issues only, or board_overview to filter issues by assignee)

issueType.description: Issue type filter (issues only), or the create screen to inspect with resource=fields (pass project too)

issueKey.description: Issue whose edit screen to inspect (resource=fields)

boardId.description: Board ID for resource=sprints or board_overview. Omit it and pass project instead: the board is resolved when the project has exactly one, otherwise the error lists the choices.

sprintState.description: Sprint state filter: active, future, closed (sprints and board_overview)

includeIssues.description: Include issues per sprint in board_overview (default true)

jira.name: jira_get
jira.description: Full details for one Jira issue: summary, description, status, assignee, sprint, available transitions, recent comments, and a list of attachments (filename, size, mime type, attachment ID). To view an attachment's contents (e.g. an image), call get_attachment with source=jira and the attachment ID surfaced here.

fullDescription.description: Return the full description even when long (default false — descriptions over ~2000 chars are truncated to save context)

jira.name: jira_mutate
jira.description: One write path for Jira: create/update a ticket, transition status, assign, sprint, comment (add/update/delete via commentAction), attach files, link issues, log work, or manage a fix version — several of them in one call. Text fields take Jira wiki markup; markdown is converted for you, so a ``` fence or **bold** still renders correctly.

issueKey.description: Existing issue key to mutate (optional if create is provided)

projectKey.description: Jira project code (optional, auto-resolved when omitted)

issueType.description: Issue type name, e.g. Bug, Story, Task, Sub-task

description.description: Issue description (optional). Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown.

reporter.description: Reporter username (optional, defaults to the caller)

components.description: Component names to apply (optional). Must already exist on the project — discover via jira_search resource=components.

fixVersion.description: Single fix version name (optional). For multiple, use fixVersions.

fixVersions.description: Fix version names (optional). Overrides fixVersion when both given.

parent.description: Parent issue key. For Sub-task issue types this sets the Jira parent. If the key points to an Epic, the Epic Link custom field is set automatically instead (Jira Server epic membership).

epicLink.description: Epic issue key to attach the new issue to as an epic child (Jira Server Epic Link). Overrides parent if both are passed.

customFields.description: Fields with no dedicated argument above, including every custom field. Keys are the field name ("Epic Name", "Story Points") or its id ("customfield_10005"). Values are plain: "text" for text, 5 for numeric, "2026-01-31" for a date, the option label for a select, the username for a user picker, and an array of labels for a multi-value field — the server wraps them into Jira's shape from the field schema. Pass an object or an array of objects to send a raw Jira value unchanged. Before creating with an unfamiliar issue type, call jira_search resource=fields project=<KEY> issueType=<TYPE>: it lists that create screen's required and optional fields with their allowed values. Epic Name defaults to summary when issueType=Epic. A rejected call answers with what the screen wants, so retry from the error rather than asking the user to use the Jira UI.

issueType.description: Change the issue type, e.g. Task → Epic (optional). Pass the new type's required fields in customFields in the same call — the type change is applied before them, so fields only the new type has (Epic Name) are accepted.

description.description: New description (optional). Use Jira wiki markup (Atlassian renderer syntax), not GitHub/CommonMark markdown.

assignee.description: New assignee username, or empty string to unassign (optional)

dueDate.description: Due date yyyy-mm-dd, or empty string to clear (optional)

components.description: Replace component set by name (pass [] to clear). Names must already exist — discover via jira_search resource=components.

fixVersion.description: Single fix version name, or empty string to clear (optional). For multiple, use fixVersions.

fixVersions.description: Replace fix version set by name (pass [] to clear). Overrides fixVersion when both given.

versions.description: Replace affects version/s set by name (pass [] to clear).

environment.description: Environment field, or empty string to clear (optional).

epicLink.description: Epic issue key to set as parent epic (Jira Server Epic Link), or empty string to clear.

customFields.description: Fields with no dedicated argument above, including every custom field. Keys are the field name ("Epic Name", "Story Points") or its id ("customfield_10005"); null clears a field. Values are plain: "text", 5, "2026-01-31", the option label for a select, the username for a user picker, an array of labels for a multi-value field — the server wraps them into Jira's shape from the field schema. Pass an object or array of objects to send a raw Jira value unchanged. Call jira_search resource=fields issueKey=<KEY> for the fields this issue's edit screen accepts, which are required, and what each select allows. A rejected call answers with what the screen wants, so retry from the error rather than asking the user to use the Jira UI.

sprintId.description: Sprint ID to add the issue into (optional)

removeFromSprint.description: Move the issue to the backlog (remove from any sprint)

transitionName.description: Transition name, e.g. "In Progress" (optional if transitionId provided)

comment.description: Comment body (optional). Added after the other mutations; with commentAction=update it is the replacement text. Markdown is converted to Jira wiki markup automatically.

commentAction.description: What to do with the comment (default: add). update/delete need commentId and only work on your own comments.

commentId.description: Comment ID (required for commentAction=update or delete)

attachments.description: Local file paths to upload as attachments on the issue (works for both newly-created and existing issues).

link.description: Create an issue link, e.g. "FOO-123 blocks BAR-456"

targetIssueKey.description: The other issue in the relationship

direction.description: outward (default): issueKey → target; inward: target → issueKey

worklog.description: Log time spent on this issue

timeSpent.description: Time in Jira format, e.g. "2h 30m" or "1d"

started.description: ISO 8601 datetime when work started (defaults to now)

version.description: Manage a fix version (release) on the project instead of an issue: create, update, release, archive, delete. Independent of issueKey. Find existing versions with jira_search resource=versions; set one on a ticket with update.fixVersion.

projectKey.description: Jira project code (create only; inherited from the top-level projectKey or the repo when omitted)

id.description: Version id (required for update/release/archive/delete; from jira_search resource=versions)

name.description: Version name, e.g. "9.1.0" (required for create; optional rename for update)

releaseDate.description: Release date in YYYY-MM-DD (optional; defaults to today on action=release)

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_search
bitbucket.description:
Discover Bitbucket resources (PRs, repos, branches, users). Set resource:
• "pull_requests" (default) — list PRs by state/branch/text; mine=true for your inbox
• "repos" — list repositories in a project
• "branches" — list or filter branches in a repo
• "users" — find users by name/email (pass query); add projectKey+repoSlug to restrict to users with repo access. Use it to resolve a person to a username before assigning them.

mine.description: Return your own PRs by role (resource=pull_requests only)

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

fromBranch.description: Filter PRs from this source branch

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_get_pr
bitbucket.description: Full details for one PR: metadata, commits, open comments, blockers, optional diff, and any attachments referenced from the description or comments (with attachment ID + filename). IMPORTANT: The PR branch is often not the locally checked-out branch. Do NOT read files with local tools (Read, git_get_context, etc.) for PR context — use bitbucket_get_file with the PR's source branch instead. To view an attachment's contents, call get_attachment with source=bitbucket and the surfaced attachment ID. The response includes a "Viewing as" line. As the author, bitbucket_comment refuses new top-level comments (replies still work) — just answer questions about the PR. As a reviewer, default to inline comments for suggested changes plus a final summary comment.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

prId.description: Pull request number (optional if fromBranch provided or running from a checked-out branch)

fromBranch.description: Source branch — auto-resolves the open PR; omit to use current checked-out branch

includeComments.description: Include review comments and blockers (default true)

includeBuildStatus.description: Include CI/build status for the head commit (default true)

commentsState.description: Comment state filter (default ALL — returns every comment with its state badge so nothing is silently hidden). Pass OPEN/RESOLVED only when explicitly narrowing.

diffCharOffset.description: Skip this many diff characters (for paging through a large diff)

fullDescription.description: Return the full PR description even when long (default false — descriptions over ~2000 chars are truncated to save context)

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_mutate
bitbucket.description: Create, update, approve/unapprove, mark needs_work, decline, or merge a PR — in one call. Auto-targets the open PR for the current branch when prId is omitted. needs_work sets your reviewer status to "Needs work" (Bitbucket Server's changes-requested signal); revert with action=unapprove.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

prId.description: Target PR number (optional, auto-resolved from branch)

action.description: Action to perform (optional — create/update are implied by a create/update object). needs_work = mark your reviewer status as "Needs work" (changes requested).

toBranch.description: Target branch (defaults to the repository default branch as Bitbucket reports it)

reviewers.description: Reviewer usernames (not display names). Each is verified against Bitbucket and the call is rejected with candidates if one does not resolve.

pickReviewers.description: Show an interactive reviewer picker before creating the PR (lists users with repo access)

description.description: Updated description, or empty string to clear (optional)

reviewers.description: Reviewer usernames. This replaces the reviewer set, so include everyone who should stay — dropping or clearing existing reviewers is rejected unless replaceReviewers=true.

replaceReviewers.description: Allow update.reviewers to remove reviewers who are currently on the PR. Only set this when the user asked for a reviewer to be removed.

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_comment
bitbucket.description: Add, update, or delete a PR comment. action defaults to "add"; a reply is action=add with commentId. Posts COMMENTS, never tasks: severity=BLOCKER is rejected on add — use bitbucket_pr_tasks (action=create) for a task, and only when the user explicitly asks. For code changes use an inline comment with suggestion whenever exact replacement code exists. Keep comments concise, no emojis (rejected). Enforced server-side, so you do not have to track it: one reply per thread per author (update your existing reply instead), no duplicate of a comment you already posted, no new top-level comment on a PR you authored (pass asAuthor=true only if the user asked for one), explanatory text only before a suggestion block, and bare "#123" references rewritten into clickable comment links. Inline comments anchor to the commits bitbucket_get_pr last showed you for that PR — remembered per session, remapped onto current head if the branch advanced — so fromHash/toHash are only needed to override that.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

commentId.description: Comment ID to reply to, update, or delete

text.description: Comment text for add/update. No filler, no emojis. If suggestion is used, keep this optional and brief; it is placed before the suggestion block.

filePath.description: File path for inline comment (must pair with line)

srcPath.description: Source path if file was renamed (optional, defaults to filePath)

line.description: Line number to anchor inline comment (must pair with filePath)

fileType.description: Diff side: TO (new, default) or FROM (old)

multilineStartLine.description: First line of multiline anchor (pair with line as last line)

fromHash.description: Override the remembered base/target commit for the anchor. Normally unnecessary: reading the PR records the pair for you.

toHash.description: Override the remembered source/feature commit for the anchor. Pair with fromHash. If the line no longer exists at current head the comment is anchored to the reviewed commit and shows as outdated, which is correct.

suggestion.description: Replacement code to suggest. Use whenever proposing a concrete code change. Posted as the final ```suggestion``` block so Apply suggestion appears. Requires filePath + line.

state.description: Task state for BLOCKER comments (update only)

severity.description: Comment severity. Leave unset — comments default to NORMAL. BLOCKER turns the comment into a task and is REJECTED on add; only pass BLOCKER on update to escalate an existing comment when the user explicitly asks. To create a task, use bitbucket_pr_tasks instead.

asAuthor.description: Allow a new top-level comment on a PR you authored. Only set this when the user explicitly asked you to comment on your own PR; replies never need it.

pending.description: Add only. Post the comment as a PENDING draft-review comment instead of publishing it immediately — it stays unpublished until the user publishes the review from the Bitbucket UI. Only set this when the user EXPLICITLY asks for a pending/draft/unpublished comment; default published behaviour otherwise.

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_get_file
bitbucket.description: Raw file content from Bitbucket at a branch, tag, or commit — the only correct source of file context for a PR whose branch is not checked out locally (local Read/git tools would show a different branch). Pass prId to read the PR source branch without looking it up, or ref for an explicit branch/tag/commit; with neither you get the repository default branch. Every response starts with the path and the ref it came from, and pages via maxChars/charOffset.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

ref.description: Branch, tag, or commit hash. Omit and pass prId to use the PR source branch; omit both for the repository default branch.

prId.description: Read the file as it is on this PR's source branch (ignored when ref is given)

charOffset.description: Skip this many characters (for paging through a large file)

bitbucket.name: bitbucket_pr_tasks
bitbucket.description: Manage PR tasks (checklist items): list, create, resolve, reopen, delete. Tasks are distinct from comments — they appear as a checklist in the PR sidebar.

repoPath.description: Local path of the repo to auto-detect project/repo from (overrides workspace roots). Usually unnecessary if projectKey+repoSlug are given.

commentId.description: Anchor the task to a specific comment ID (optional for create)

combined.name: complete_work
combined.description: Close the loop on a finished branch: merges the open PR and transitions the Jira ticket to Done (or a named transition). Mirrors start_work. Refuses to merge while reviewers have not approved or a build on the PR head has failed — pass force=true to merge anyway.

issueKey.description: Jira issue key to transition (auto-detected from branch name if omitted)

prId.description: PR to merge (auto-detected from current branch if omitted)

transitionName.description: Jira transition to apply after merge (default: "Done")

skipJiraTransition.description: Skip transitioning the Jira ticket (default false)

force.description: Merge even though reviewers have not approved or a build failed. Only when the user says to merge anyway.
